subject.title: [Bug]: Config validator rejects mediaLocalRoots despite type definitions supporting it (Telegram outbound)

question: Should OpenClaw solve remaining local outbound media root needs through a canonical `tools.fs.roots`-style filesystem policy, keep the current fs-read trust model only, or add a narrower `mediaLocalRoots` config surface?
rationale: The remaining work changes which host paths an agent can read and transmit as media, so automation cannot safely choose the permanent config/security boundary from source inspection alone.

options.title: Canonical filesystem roots
options.body: Use a shared `tools.fs.roots`-style policy for host path access and make outbound media consume that one root model after security review.

options.title: Keep current fs-read model
options.body: Close this class of requests as covered by `tools.fs.workspaceOnly=false` plus read policy, accepting that there is no narrower root allowlist today.

options.title: Add mediaLocalRoots
options.body: Expose a media-specific root allowlist under channel or agent config, accepting a second policy surface that must be documented, tested, and migrated carefully.

recommendation.title: Canonical filesystem roots
recommendation.body: Use a shared `tools.fs.roots`-style policy for host path access and make outbound media consume that one root model after security review.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter introduced the current media access path and docs that this decision would extend or intentionally leave as-is.
